questions.objective: Decide whether to update firmware using compatibility and recovery evidence.
questions.prompt: A supported security update prohibits downgrade. Which statements are justified? Select all that apply.
options: Document the unsupported rollback boundary.
Test and arrange a supported recovery or replacement route.
Promise a reverse update to reassure the reviewer.
Ignore the update because every change must be reversible in software.
explanations: The real limitation belongs in the change decision.
Recovery may require a different supported method, local access or replacement.
An invented rollback creates false confidence.
A non-downgradable update can still be justified through risk and recovery planning.

questions.objective: Accept commissioning only after independent function and recovery checks.
questions.prompt: The firmware updater reports success. What is still required before release?
options: Close the task immediately.
Validate identity, approved settings, management restrictions, host function and recovery evidence.
Reboot repeatedly without a test plan.
Delete the previous baseline and logs.
explanations: Update completion does not establish system acceptance.
Commissioning tests the resulting operational and trust state.
Unplanned reboots can create disruption without useful evidence.
Previous evidence is essential to understanding the change and recovery.

questions.objective: Calculate usable capacity and reserve without confusing raw device ratings.
questions.prompt: Eight 4 TB active members form a conventional RAID 6 group; one additional 4 TB drive is a hot spare. What is nominal group data capacity before reserves and formatting?
options: 36 TB
32 TB
24 TB
20 TB
explanations: This counts all installed raw media, including parity and spare.
This is active raw capacity before parity allowance.
(8 − 2) × 4 TB = 24 TB nominal data capacity.
This subtracts three active-device equivalents without the stated reason.

questions.objective: Compare redundancy, replication, snapshots and independent backups.
questions.prompt: A snapshot is stored on the same array and controlled by the same compromised administrator. What restoration claim is justified?
options: It guarantees recovery from destruction of that array.
It is automatically independent of the compromised control plane.
Its usefulness depends on surviving shared media and administrative failure; an independent restore route is still needed.
Snapshots can never support any recovery.
explanations: The snapshot shares the array’s failure exposure.
Shared administrative authority may affect both current and historical data.
Assess the actual failure and trust boundaries rather than the feature name.
Snapshots can be useful within their supported failure scope.

questions.objective: Assess controller caching, endurance and acknowledged-write protection.
questions.prompt: Controller cache protection fails and the supported controller switches to a slower protected policy. What should happen?
options: Force unsafe caching to recover the benchmark number.
Assess the supported degraded mode and service impact, repair protection and retest.
Declare every acknowledged write lost without evidence.
Ignore the alert because all disks are online.
explanations: Performance does not justify defeating required write integrity.
The decision must preserve supported integrity while addressing capacity and repair.
The controller may preserve integrity by changing policy; inspect evidence.
Disk presence does not establish controller cache health.

questions.objective: Validate multipath service with an application-level failure test.
questions.prompt: Two storage paths are visible, but both use one switch. Which statements are justified? Select all that apply.
options: The switch is a common dependency.
A safe application I/O failure test is needed for the required service criterion.
Two paths prove survival of switch loss.
A successful ping after recovery proves no data interruption occurred.
explanations: Both paths can fail with the shared switch.
The service requirement concerns I/O continuity, timing and integrity.
Path count does not establish independent failure domains.
Ping does not measure historical application continuity or data integrity.

questions.objective: Evaluate remaining fault tolerance during replacement and rebuild.
questions.prompt: One member of a conventional RAID 5 group has failed and rebuild is incomplete. How much tolerance remains for another complete member failure in that group?
options: Two more drives
One more drive
No further complete member failure under that model
Unlimited if a hot spare was present
explanations: RAID 5 does not provide this member-failure tolerance.
The single complete-member margin is already consumed.
The degraded group has consumed its complete-member redundancy.
A spare starts replacement/rebuild; it is not instant restored redundancy.

questions.objective: Accept storage repair only after integrity and independent restoration tests.
questions.prompt: A controller replacement restores a green array. What best closes the repair and recovery evidence?
options: Only the green status screenshot
An undocumented reinitialisation of every disk
Passing integrity/application/protection tests plus a separately demonstrated backup restoration
A note that RAID is a backup
explanations: Status is one observation and cannot prove full integrity or recoverability.
Reinitialisation can destroy required configuration and data.
Repair and independent recovery have distinct acceptance criteria.
RAID handles specified failures; it is not an independent backup.

questions.objective: Define a reproducible supported host and driver baseline.
questions.prompt: Which item most directly undermines a claimed reproducible host build?
options: A versioned media and driver manifest
A required unrecorded file available only on the original engineer’s laptop
Documented secret retrieval through the approved vault
A repeated installation on a clean authorised node
explanations: Versioned inputs support repeatability.
The hidden dependency prevents another operator from reliably reproducing the build.
Secrets should be retrieved securely rather than committed into scripts.
A repeat test provides evidence of reproducibility.

questions.objective: Trace DNS, time, identity, storage and database dependencies.
questions.prompt: The credentials required to restore the identity server can be retrieved only after that identity server works. What is this?
options: A sufficient recovery design
A circular recovery dependency requiring an independent approved access route
Proof that identity is unnecessary
A reason to publish all passwords in the repository
explanations: The failed service blocks access needed to recover itself.
The loop needs protected emergency access and a tested recovery procedure.
Identity remains necessary; its recovery dependencies need redesign.
Publishing credentials creates exposure and is not an approved recovery mechanism.

questions.objective: Validate least-privilege service accounts and management agents.
questions.prompt: A monitoring agent reports green, but the historian service account cannot write to its database. Which conclusion is supported?
options: All application functions are healthy.
The agent’s observation does not establish the service account’s required permissions or transaction success.
The agent must be malicious.
Grant every account administrator rights.
explanations: Agent status covers only what it actually observes.
Validate the application identity and transaction directly.
A coverage gap does not establish malicious activity.
Broad privilege escalation fails least privilege and may not solve the actual fault.

questions.objective: Distinguish a virtual-machine boot from restored infrastructure service.
questions.prompt: A recovered VM boots and responds to ping. What is still needed for an OT historian acceptance claim?
options: Only a desktop screenshot
Current-value ingestion, historical-data reads, correct time interpretation and authorised/denied access tests
A successful hypervisor heartbeat with no application transactions
An extra reboot with no observations
explanations: A desktop does not demonstrate historian function.
These tests exercise the required service and its trust boundaries.
Heartbeat supports guest liveness but not historian data, timing or role correctness.
An unplanned reboot adds little evidence and may disrupt recovery.

questions.objective: Use dependency evidence to accept or reject a hardware-replacement diagnosis.
questions.prompt: Disk health and I/O are normal, but service logs show login failure immediately after a credential change. What is the strongest next action?
options: Replace all drives.
Investigate the service identity and credential reference using approved diagnostics.
Disable all authentication.
Declare the host recovered because the hardware is healthy.
explanations: The observations do not currently support a disk-replacement diagnosis.
The timeline and observed failure point discriminate the identity hypothesis.
Disabling authentication violates required access controls.
Healthy hardware alone does not restore the failed service.

questions.objective: Restore required service and data in a justified dependency order.
questions.prompt: Which measurements belong in a host-loss restoration assessment? Select all that apply.
options: Time to accepted required service, including dependency delays
Correct current and retained data plus intended administrative authority
Only the time until the first boot logo
Only the number of files in the backup folder
explanations: The restoration objective concerns usable accepted service, not a selected easy interval.
Data and control are necessary parts of the recovered function.
Boot is only an intermediate milestone.
File count does not establish correctness, access or recoverability.

questions.objective: Derive acceptance tests and stop limits from requirements before execution.
questions.prompt: A team starts a maximum-load test before deciding thermal stop limits. What is the appropriate response?
options: Continue and choose limits after seeing the result.
Stop or hold execution until approved limits, monitoring and authority are defined.
Use only the processor thermal limit and leave chassis, GPU and service limits undefined.
Treat the highest observed temperature as automatically acceptable.
explanations: Post-hoc limits can rationalise an unacceptable result and leave the test uncontrolled.
A bounded test requires predefined safe and service limits.
One component limit does not bound the whole system or its service behaviour.
Observation alone does not establish an approved limit.

questions.objective: Interpret latency, throughput and error measurements with stated conditions.
questions.prompt: A trial has 99 requests at 2 ms and one at 202 ms; the maximum allowed is 100 ms. Which result is correct?
options: Mean 4 ms and the maximum criterion passes.
Mean 4 ms and the maximum criterion fails.
Mean 202 ms and the criterion passes.
No latency conclusion can be drawn from recorded samples.
explanations: A low mean does not erase the 202 ms violation.
The arithmetic mean is 4 ms, but one sample exceeds the specified maximum.
The maximum is 202 ms; that is not the mean and it exceeds the limit.
The defined trial provides enough evidence to identify this violation.

questions.objective: Correlate memory, PCIe, NIC, GPU and thermal evidence.
questions.prompt: A throughput drop coincides with bus-link retraining while thermal evidence remains within the approved envelope. Which next observation is most discriminating?
options: Compare expected and negotiated PCIe width/generation and associated logs.
Replace the fan assembly solely because the transfer result is low.
Replace every GPU without preserving logs.
Ignore the bus events because averages are normal.
explanations: Topology and link events directly test a plausible path problem.
The recorded thermal evidence does not yet support a fan diagnosis; investigate the correlated bus-path evidence.
Unfocused replacement loses evidence and may reproduce the fault.
Correlated events can matter even when averages conceal them.

questions.objective: Distinguish hardware faults from configuration, software and upstream causes.
questions.prompt: A remote transfer is slow. Which statements are justified? Select all that apply.
options: A supported local transfer test can help separate host/device limits from remote-path effects.
Source storage, NUMA placement and network congestion are competing causes.
Slow transfer proves the GPU is defective.
A reboot that improves performance proves the original cause was hardware.
explanations: A controlled comparison can distinguish where a bottleneck lies.
The end-to-end transfer depends on several layers.
Performance alone does not identify the faulty layer.
Reboots change many states and do not isolate a cause.

questions.objective: Design a safe discriminating fault experiment and preserve raw results.
questions.prompt: Which fault exercise is suitable when physical thermal fault injection is not authorised?
options: Block the live server’s air intake.
Disable shutdown protection.
Use an instructor-provided labelled thermal trace for reasoning and keep physical validation open.
Claim a paper trace is a measured production fault.
explanations: Obstructing cooling can violate the approved equipment envelope.
Protective functions are not disabled for an unauthorised experiment.
A synthetic or supplied trace supports diagnosis learning without misrepresenting evidence.
Evidence fidelity must be stated accurately.

questions.objective: Justify release or hold after correction and representative retesting.
questions.prompt: A correction makes one benchmark pass. What best supports release?
options: Retain only the latest passing score and omit the earlier test conditions.
Repeat the relevant failed and affected functional tests under comparable conditions, then assess predefined criteria.
Approve every future workload automatically.
Accept without checking that the new configuration is supported.
explanations: Without comparable conditions and failed evidence, the reviewer cannot establish what the correction changed.
Retesting establishes the corrected result and relevant side effects.
One bounded test cannot establish unrestricted performance.
Support and compatibility remain acceptance requirements.

questions.objective: Build an operating record that reconciles physical and management inventory.
questions.prompt: A replaced server board leaves a new BMC identity but the asset system retains the old identity without explanation. What must happen?
options: Ignore it because the hostname is unchanged.
Reconcile the physical, management, support and asset records with the authorised replacement.
Change the hardware’s identity arbitrarily to match the spreadsheet.
Delete the maintenance history.
explanations: Hostname continuity does not resolve hardware identity and support traceability.
The record must connect old and new components and the actual service.
Identity should be accurately recorded, not fabricated.
History explains the change and is needed for later review.

questions.objective: Interpret cumulative counters, rates and missing telemetry correctly.
questions.prompt: A cumulative counter falls from 900 to 4 after a reboot. How should the rate calculation handle it?
options: Report −896 errors as a health improvement.
Mark the reset and start a new comparable interval.
Add 900 fictional errors to preserve the graph.
Assume the sensor is permanently unusable.
explanations: Negative errors are an artefact of crossing a reset boundary.
Counter semantics and reset context are needed for meaningful rates.
Fabricated events would corrupt the record.
The sensor may remain useful once its reset behaviour is handled.

questions.objective: Evaluate ECC, storage endurance and path-error trends against model-specific guidance.
questions.prompt: Corrected ECC events accelerate at one reported location. Which statement is best?
options: Corrected events never require investigation.
Replace after exactly ten events on every platform.
Investigate mapping, trends and competing causes using applicable OEM guidance.
Disable ECC reporting to restore a green dashboard.
explanations: Correction does not establish that continued deterioration is harmless.
Universal thresholds ignore model-specific reporting and guidance.
The decision needs actual event context and supported interpretation.
Suppressing evidence does not resolve the underlying condition.

questions.objective: Prioritise maintenance using consequence, exposure and recovery capability.
questions.prompt: A drive is deteriorating while its array is already degraded. Which factors should influence maintenance priority? Select all that apply.
options: Remaining protection and data-service consequence
Suitable spare lead time and verified independent recovery
Only whether the supplier has a generally strong reliability reputation
Only whether the dashboard average is green
explanations: The same warning has different consequence when protection is reduced.
Repair and recovery capability affect exposure and the appropriate schedule.
General reputation does not establish the current device condition, exposure or recovery route.
Averages and status summaries can hide the relevant deterioration.

questions.objective: Review firmware or configuration changes through controlled evidence.
questions.prompt: A compliance report labels every device below the newest firmware noncompliant. What is missing?
options: A supported approved baseline, applicable advisories and reviewed exceptions per configuration
A more frequent scan that still compares only with the newest release
Permission to bypass all staging tests
A universal rule that older firmware is always safer
explanations: Compliance is against the approved supported requirement, informed by actual risk and dependencies.
Frequency does not correct the missing supported, configuration-specific baseline.
Staging remains important for controlled change.
Neither old nor new is inherently appropriate without context.

questions.objective: Verify recurrence and effectiveness after maintenance or improvement.
questions.prompt: No warning recurs after maintenance, but telemetry collection stopped during the same period. What can be accepted?
options: The maintenance has conclusively eliminated the fault.
Only that no observations were collected; restore monitoring and complete the defined retest.
The absence of data is proof of zero errors.
All future maintenance can be cancelled.
explanations: No observation cannot establish absence of recurrence.
The effectiveness criterion remains untested until valid monitoring resumes.
Zero and missing data have different meanings.
Future plans require evidence, not an observability gap.

questions.objective: Assess service exposure and authority before a hardware maintenance action.
questions.prompt: A server has a suspect fan while another required cooling component is already unavailable. What should the work order evaluate first?
options: Only the fan’s purchase price
Current service exposure, permitted maintenance state and authorised supported method
How quickly a technician can pull the module
Whether the technician has completed a similar repair on another model
explanations: Cost alone does not establish whether the current state permits the work.
Existing degradation changes the consequence and permissible method.
Speed does not replace a safe supported maintenance plan.
Past experience does not establish that this model and current degraded state permit the proposed work.

questions.objective: Identify a supported FRU and model-specific hot or cold replacement method.
questions.prompt: A memory module has an accessible latch. Does this establish hot-swap permission?
options: Yes, because accessible parts are always hot-swappable.
No; the exact model and configuration procedure determines the required state.
Yes, if the BMC remains reachable.
No memory module can ever be serviced by anyone.
explanations: Mechanical accessibility does not establish live-removal support.
Use the supported procedure and verify isolation where required.
BMC reachability does not prove a memory-service state is permitted.
Authorised supported service is possible, but not inferred from appearance.

questions.objective: Verify the intended component and isolation state before removal.
questions.prompt: The identify light indicates bay 4 but the work order lists the serial now observed in bay 5. What should happen?
options: Pull bay 4 immediately.
Pull both bays to avoid ambiguity.
Stop and reconcile current physical identity and diagnostic evidence before removal.
Edit the work order afterward to match whichever part was removed.
explanations: The conflicting identity must be resolved before action.
Removing additional parts can destroy remaining protection.
Multiple identifiers prevent an avoidable wrong-component removal.
Retrospective edits do not authorise the action or resolve the initial discrepancy.

questions.objective: Coordinate drive, memory, NIC, fan, PSU and accelerator replacement differences.
questions.prompt: A replacement HBA is detected by the OS but has a new WWN. What remains to be checked?
options: Only that the replacement was supplied in OEM packaging
Approved storage access, mapping, multipath behaviour and actual application I/O
Only whether the server boots
Nothing; HBA identities never affect storage access
explanations: Provenance matters, but it does not demonstrate storage identity, mapping and actual I/O.
Changed identity can affect access and integration despite successful enumeration.
Boot may use a different path from the required application storage.
Storage access often depends on initiator identity and configuration.

questions.objective: Reject an incompatible part or unsupported replacement proposal.
questions.prompt: A required workload draws 1.5 kW at the PSU DC outputs; either remaining PSU supplies at most 1.2 kW DC under the stated conditions. Which proposal is justified?
options: Remove one supply at full required load because two are installed.
Hold that live-removal plan and arrange a supported workload reduction or shutdown.
Ignore the measurements because the PSU is new.
Approve removal because the two installed nameplate ratings total 2.4 kW.
explanations: The remaining supply cannot meet the stated demand.
The maintenance method must satisfy capacity and OEM operating rules.
Age does not change the demonstrated capacity requirement.
The maintenance state has only one remaining module; the original combined capacity is not available then.

questions.objective: Accept return to service only after physical and functional retesting.
questions.prompt: Which evidence is needed after an authorised FRU replacement? Select all that apply.
options: Physical and inventory checks for the correct installed component
Required functional tests, restored protection and recurrence observation
Only the shipping receipt
Only a quiz score about the component
explanations: The record must show which part is actually installed and correctly integrated.
Return to service includes behaviour and the intended protection state.
A receipt proves procurement, not installation or recovery.
Knowledge evidence does not demonstrate physical work.

questions.objective: Define restoration objectives and a dependency-aware recovery sequence.
questions.prompt: Hardware preparation takes 15 minutes and network preparation 12 minutes in parallel; restore takes 25 minutes afterward and acceptance 10 more. What is the planned critical path?
options: 62 minutes
50 minutes
37 minutes
25 minutes
explanations: Adding both parallel tasks overstates their combined elapsed time.
This omits a required phase or combines dependencies incorrectly.
Restoration alone excludes prerequisite and acceptance time.

questions.objective: Distinguish host, boot-media, controller, firmware and management failure routes.
questions.prompt: After controller failure, the replacement utility offers to initialise all attached drives. The supported recovery procedure has not been checked. What should happen?
options: Initialise immediately to make the status green.
Hold the action, preserve identities/configuration evidence and obtain the supported recovery method.
Assume every controller imports every array automatically.
Discard the backup because physical disks are still present.
explanations: Initialisation can destroy required configuration or data.
Controller recovery must preserve the relevant data and follow supported instructions.
Compatibility and import procedures vary.
Physical media survival does not establish readable or consistent data.

questions.objective: Preserve data and identity during supported configuration recovery.
questions.prompt: A replacement motherboard changes access to a TPM-sealed recovery secret. What should the plan have included?
options: An independently protected approved recovery-key route and a tested platform-change procedure
Only another copy of the same inaccessible encrypted file
A rule that all motherboard swaps preserve every key automatically
Publication of all recovery secrets in GitHub
explanations: Platform changes can affect sealed access, so recovery dependencies must be arranged and tested.
Another inaccessible copy does not remove the dependency.
Protected-key behaviour depends on the implementation and policy.
Secrets require authorised protection, not public distribution.

questions.objective: Restore trusted administrative authority as well as service availability.
questions.prompt: The application works after rebuilding, but a default BMC administrator remains enabled contrary to requirements. What is the correct result?
options: Recovery is fully accepted because the web page loads.
Availability may be restored, but the required administrative-trust criterion remains open.
Delete all logs and ignore the account.
Disable every account including approved recovery access.
explanations: Service availability alone does not meet the trust requirement.
Correct access and verify intended and denied operations before full acceptance.
Removing evidence does not correct the exposure.
Recovery must preserve approved control while removing unauthorised access.

questions.objective: Plan refresh and migration around compatibility, reduced protection and fallback.
questions.prompt: A refresh plan says “switch back to the old node” after users have written new data on the target. What is missing?
options: Only the old node's successful pre-migration diagnostic result
A defined authoritative data set, consistency/reconciliation process and decision deadline
An unconditional assumption that both copies are identical
Permission to erase both nodes
explanations: A healthy old node does not establish that its data remains authoritative after writes on the target.
Fallback after writes requires a supported data-consistency plan.
Post-cutover writes can make the old state stale.
Erasing both systems is not a recovery plan.

questions.objective: Reject partial restoration claims using functional, integrity and timing evidence.
questions.prompt: Which results are required before accepting the recovered hardware service? Select all that apply.
options: Required current and retained data, functional performance and remaining protection
Intended administrative authority and measured end-to-end restoration time
Only the first successful ping
Only a firmware installation-success message
explanations: These establish the required usable data service and hardware state.
Trust and time are independent mandatory dimensions of the recovery claim.
Ping cannot prove data, permissions or application function.
An update message does not establish full restoration.

questions.objective: Identify retained-service dependencies before relocation or retirement.
questions.prompt: An old server is scheduled for retirement but holds the only backup catalogue and recovery key access path. What must happen first?
options: Destroy its disks to reduce clutter.
Move and test the required recovery dependencies through an approved process before release.
Mark the asset inactive and assume recovery is unaffected.
Copy the keys into a public portfolio document.
explanations: Destruction would remove required continuing-service dependencies.
Retirement must preserve tested recovery capability before eliminating the old source.
Administrative status does not move the dependency.
Recovery material must remain protected through approved mechanisms.

questions.objective: Select an approved media-sanitisation method for the actual device and destination.
questions.prompt: A quick format leaves an SSD’s filesystem empty. Which claim is justified?
options: Every remapped physical location is proven sanitised.
The filesystem appears empty; the required sanitisation outcome still needs an approved supported method and evidence.
The device has definitely been physically destroyed.
All encryption keys everywhere have been revoked.
explanations: Host-visible formatting does not establish all physical media coverage.
The observation is narrower than a sanitisation acceptance decision.
Formatting does not physically destroy the device.
Filesystem state does not establish external key or identity state.

questions.objective: Distinguish operation verification from the final sanitisation acceptance decision.
questions.prompt: A tool reports successful sanitisation but no device identifier was retained. What is missing?
options: Only a second screenshot of the same unidentified success message
Traceability that proves which required asset received the approved completed process
Permission to copy the same result to every asset
Nothing; one success message covers the whole batch
explanations: Repeating an unbound result does not establish the device identity or asset traceability.
Process evidence must be tied to the actual device and disposition requirement.
Reusing one result would fabricate evidence for other assets.
A single unbound result cannot establish batch completion.

questions.objective: Assess cryptographic-erase prerequisites and residual key dependencies.
questions.prompt: Before accepting a cryptographic-erase method, which factors matter? Select all that apply.
options: Whether the relevant data was protected by the required encryption and implementation
Whether usable relevant keys or copies remain accessible outside the erased location
Only whether the user account password changed
Only whether the disk label contains the word encrypted
explanations: The method relies on applicable encryption and implementation prerequisites.
Remaining usable key material can defeat the intended result.
An account password is not necessarily the data-encryption key or all of its copies.
A label is not evidence of the required cryptographic state.

questions.objective: Remove management identities and reconcile custody beyond the main data disks.
questions.prompt: All main data drives have accepted records, but the retired BMC still accepts its previous administrative account. What follows?
options: The complete asset retirement claim remains open until required management reset/revocation and verification are performed.
Disk sanitisation automatically disables every BMC account.
The account is harmless because a cable is currently unplugged.
Approve retirement because the next owner is expected to change the BMC password
explanations: Retirement includes applicable residual management data and identity requirements.
The BMC is a separate management subsystem.
Disconnection does not revoke credentials or establish future access state.
A future expectation does not meet the current required reset and revocation criterion.

questions.objective: Release a retired asset only after evidence supports every required disposition criterion.
questions.prompt: Eleven of twelve drives have matched accepted sanitisation records. One drive’s identity is unresolved. What is the appropriate batch disposition?
options: Round 91.7% to 100% and release every drive.
Hold the unresolved item and reconcile identity, method evidence and custody before its release.
Assume the missing drive is the safest one.
Claim physical destruction without observing or receiving traceable evidence.
explanations: Percentages cannot waive an individual mandatory disposition requirement.
Each asset needs a supported traceable release decision.
No evidence supports that assumption.
Unseen or undocumented destruction cannot be claimed.

questions.objective: Evidence / verification chain
questions.prompt: A corrected configuration is committed after a failed alarm test. What closes the defect?
options: The commit timestamp
A passing retest tied to the implemented revision and original criterion
Deleting the failed result
A higher quiz score
explanations: A commit proves a recorded change, not operating behaviour.
The retest connects the corrected implementation to the required result.
The failed result explains the defect and must remain in history.
Knowledge scores do not test the deployed configuration.

questions.objective: Evidence / environment claims
questions.prompt: A digital rack model correctly predicts cable reach. Which claim is defensible?
options: The real server was installed correctly
Physical cable workmanship is certified
The geometry was checked within the model assumptions
Production commissioning is complete
explanations: The model does not observe installation.
Workmanship needs appropriate physical inspection and tests.
This states the demonstrated analytical boundary.
Commissioning requires actual functional evidence and authority.

questions.objective: Evidence / integrity
questions.prompt: Two exported logs have matching hashes before and after transfer. What does that establish?
options: The sensors were calibrated
The bytes checked by the hashes are unchanged
The operator had site authority
The timestamps are accurate
explanations: Calibration requires its own evidence.
A matching appropriate digest checks byte integrity, subject to its method.
Authority is separate from file integrity.
A preserved timestamp can still originate from a wrong clock.

questions.objective: Evidence / programme identifiers
questions.prompt: A learner completes an Advanced lesson about modelling. What automatically follows?
options: Portfolio Release 5 acceptance
Long-term D2/D3 competence
Completion of the app learning activity only, subject to its gate
CCIE award
explanations: Release 5 has independent evidence and review requirements.
Additional specialist teaching and physical work remain necessary.
The milestone stays at the level actually demonstrated.
Only the provider awards its credential.

questions.objective: Evidence / negative tests
questions.prompt: An access-control requirement says an unauthorised user cannot alter setpoints. Which evidence is needed?
options: Only a successful administrator edit
A colour-coded role diagram
An authorised negative test of the disallowed operation, plus required allowed operations
An unrelated equipment health report
explanations: Allowed behaviour does not establish denied behaviour.
A diagram states intention.
Both boundary and legitimate function should be verified in a controlled environment.
Hardware health does not test access enforcement.

questions.objective: Evidence / independence
questions.prompt: The implementer labels their own run reviewed. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Independent acceptance is complete
The run is self-reported until the stated review requirement is met
All raw data must be discarded
The implementation is necessarily faulty
explanations: Self-review and independent review are different.
Preserve the useful result with an honest review state.
The original data can support later review.
Review status alone does not determine technical correctness.

questions.objective: Power / maintenance capacity
questions.prompt: Three 500 kW usable modules serve 850 kW. One is in maintenance and a second fails. What is the arithmetic result?
options: 650 kW headroom
150 kW headroom
350 kW shortfall
The load halves automatically
explanations: That uses all three installed modules.
That uses two modules, but only one remains.
Demand does not disappear unless an approved curtailment action changes it.

questions.objective: Power / common causes
questions.prompt: Two rack feeds share one upstream bypass. What is the best conclusion?
options: Different feed names establish independence
The shared bypass is a dependency to analyse against required failures and maintenance
The bypass must be operated immediately
All dual-corded devices are defective
explanations: Labels do not change topology.
Its modes and exposure may affect both paths.
A review finding is not switching authority.
The issue concerns the supplied paths and requirement, not necessarily the device.

questions.objective: Power / energy screen
questions.prompt: An ideal 600 kW load needs 20 seconds of stored energy. What is the minimum ideal energy before losses?
options: 3.33 kWh
30 kWh
0.03 kWh
explanations: Seconds must be converted to hours.
600 × 20/3600 = 3.33 kWh; real selection needs manufacturer performance data.
Dividing power by time is not energy.
The time conversion is incorrect.

questions.objective: Power / measurement bandwidth
questions.prompt: A 15-minute average remains below a limit but workload ramps are suspected. What is missing?
options: A larger dashboard font
A demand trace with adequate sampling, timing and bandwidth for the event
A claim that the average is instantaneous
Only the monthly electricity bill
explanations: Presentation cannot recover unmeasured dynamics.
The measurement must resolve the phenomenon being assessed.
That misstates the observation.
Billing energy does not resolve short ramps.

questions.objective: Power / release authority
questions.prompt: A simple capacity model shows positive headroom. What can the learner approve from that alone?
options: Protection coordination
Any live switching sequence
Only the stated arithmetic screening result within its assumptions
The entire electrical installation
explanations: The model omits fault/protection behaviour.
Switching needs the applicable authority and procedure.
This is the demonstrated analytical boundary.
Many required design and physical tests remain outside the model.

questions.objective: Power / restart dependencies
questions.prompt: After an outage, restored power is available but cooling status is unverified. What is the strongest next decision?
options: Restart every rack simultaneously
Follow the approved dependency order and verify cooling/control readiness before the permitted restart stages
Hide cooling alarms
Assume power restoration proves all services are ready
explanations: That can exceed capacity or thermal limits.
Restoration must establish dependent readiness and bounded demand.
Removing information does not restore function.
Power is one dependency among several.

questions.objective: Cooling / heat balance
questions.prompt: For assumed water properties, 2 kg/s at 4.18 kJ/(kg·K) and a 5 K rise gives what heat estimate?
options: 418 kWh
explanations: The scale is wrong.
This equation gives power, not accumulated energy.
The temperature rise is multiplied, not divided.

questions.objective: Cooling / local capacity
questions.prompt: Total liquid flow is normal but one rack is overheating. What conclusion is justified?
options: All branch flows must be normal
The total does not establish adequate delivery to that branch
The rack sensor must be wrong
Increasing every pump is automatically approved
explanations: Parallel distribution can be unequal.
Check branch conditions and valid local observations.
Sensor error is possible but needs evidence.
Actions depend on the approved sequence and limits.

questions.objective: Cooling / sensor uncertainty
questions.prompt: Two temperature sensors each have ±0.2 K bounded uncertainty. What conservative worst-case bound applies to their difference?
options: Always ±0.04 K
explanations: Errors need not cancel.
One sensor alone does not bound the difference.
Opposite extreme errors can add to 0.4 K.
That precision is unsupported.

questions.objective: Cooling / transient validation
questions.prompt: A cooling model matches steady-state data. May it approve a rapid workload ramp?
options: Yes, every model is dynamic
Only after its transient response is validated for the intended ramp and conditions
Yes, if its chart is smooth
No model can ever inform an engineering decision
explanations: Steady balance does not identify delays and dynamic response.
Validation must match intended use.
Visual smoothness is not a measured transient comparison.
Validated bounded models can inform decisions.

questions.objective: Cooling / evidence boundary
questions.prompt: A CFD plot predicts acceptable rack inlet temperature. Which evidence is still needed to claim as-built performance?
options: Only a more colourful plot
Appropriate physical measurements under the declared test states
A quiz about airflow
An unrelated network ping
explanations: Rendering does not add physical validation.
As-built performance requires observations and a suitable test plan.
Knowledge is a separate milestone.
Reachability does not measure airflow or temperature.

questions.objective: Cooling / restored function
questions.prompt: After a filter replacement, the work order says complete but rack temperature remains above its approved limit. What disposition fits?
options: Close because the part was changed
Hold return-to-service acceptance and investigate the unmet functional criterion
Delete the temperature history
Declare the limit irrelevant
explanations: Task execution does not establish restored service.
Acceptance follows required behaviour, not effort expended.
History is relevant evidence.
Only the authorised requirement process can change the limit.

questions.objective: Operations / commissioning scope
questions.prompt: A pump controller powers on and accepts its configuration. What is still required?
options: Nothing; power-on is commissioning
Tests of approved sequence, signals, abnormal states and dependent function
Only a serial-number photograph
A higher purchase price
explanations: Power-on is a component observation.
Commissioning checks intended system behaviour and boundaries.
Identity evidence is useful but insufficient.
Price does not establish function.

questions.objective: Operations / CMMS closure
questions.prompt: A replacement part was fitted but its service fails the acceptance test. How should the record read?
options: Work action performed; return-to-service acceptance held pending correction and retest
All complete because effort was spent
Delete the failed test
Move the asset to another name
explanations: This preserves both the performed action and the unmet criterion.
Effort is not restored function.
Failure history supports diagnosis and review.
Renaming does not correct the defect.

questions.objective: Operations / rollback dependency
questions.prompt: A rollback image is available only through the identity server being replaced. What is the concern?
options: No concern if the filename is correct
The recovery path may fail with the changed dependency
The backup is necessarily malware
The change is automatically forbidden forever
explanations: Availability under the failure matters.
Test independent authorised access to the required recovery artefacts.
The evidence shows an access dependency, not malware.
The design can be corrected and retested.

questions.objective: Operations / spares
questions.prompt: A spare controller is physically present. Which additional checks matter?
options: Compatibility, supported configuration/licence and validated restoration method
Only its packaging colour
Only that it has the same number of LEDs
None until an incident
explanations: A usable spare must work in the actual recovery path.
Packaging is not functional compatibility.
Appearance cannot establish support or behaviour.
Preparation before failure is part of readiness.

questions.objective: Operations / service metrics
questions.prompt: Two repair events average 20 minutes. What is a defensible report?
options: Every future repair will take 20 minutes
The observed mean is 20 minutes for two stated events; general predictive confidence is limited
The system has zero failure risk
All incidents have the same cause
explanations: A small historical sample cannot guarantee future duration.
State sample, definitions and limits.
Repair duration does not establish failure probability.
Different causes can have different repair paths.

questions.objective: Operations / handover
questions.prompt: A temporary alarm suppression remains active at shift change. What must happen?
options: Omit it to keep the report short
Record its scope, reason, owner, expiry and compensating checks in handover
Delete the alarm configuration
Treat the absence of alarms as proof of health
explanations: The next shift needs the degraded-observation state.
Temporary changes must remain visible and governed.
Deletion can destroy the intended alarm function.
Suppression changes visibility, not equipment state.

questions.objective: Facility / external ownership
questions.prompt: A rack loading proposal lacks an approved floor-load envelope. What is the correct response?
options: Infer approval from floor appearance
Hold the interface decision and obtain the responsible specialist evidence
Claim D1 structural competence from the app
Proceed because the rack fits in plan view
explanations: Appearance cannot establish structural capacity.
The missing external requirement must be resolved by its owner.
D1 is excluded and app study does not create authority.
Geometric fit does not establish load or route suitability.

questions.objective: Facility / standards claims
questions.prompt: A supplier writes standards compliant without an edition or scope. What is missing?
options: Only a logo
Applicable source/version, requirement mapping and supporting evidence
An unrelated certification badge
Nothing if the supplier is large
explanations: Branding does not define compliance.
These make the claim reviewable.
A different credential may cover different scope.
Supplier size does not replace evidence.

questions.objective: Facility / pathway diversity
questions.prompt: Two uplinks run through the same conduit. What can be claimed?
options: Complete physical diversity
Two links with a shared route dependency
Immunity to excavation damage
Certified optical loss margin
explanations: A common conduit is a shared exposure.
This states the actual topology.
One route event may affect both.
Optical margin requires the appropriate test.

questions.objective: Facility / fire interface
questions.prompt: BMS stops receiving fire-panel status. What must remain distinct?
options: The display interface and the independently designed protective function
Only the colour of the alarm
All protection and BMS are necessarily the same system
Network staff may bypass fire protection to test it
explanations: Diagnose the interface while preserving specialist protection authority.
Colour does not establish function.
The approved architecture defines the separation.
Testing requires the relevant authorisation and safe procedure.

questions.objective: Facility / maintainability
questions.prompt: A server fits the rack but its field-replaceable unit cannot be removed with the permitted service clearance. What is the finding?
options: Capacity is fully accepted because rack units fit
The proposed arrangement fails its maintenance interface requirement
A firmware update fixes clearance
Only cosmetic improvement is needed
explanations: Physical fit is only one requirement.
Serviceability is a lifecycle design constraint.
Software cannot create physical clearance.
The consequence affects restoration and work methods.

questions.objective: Facility / rating scope
questions.prompt: A component has a product certificate. Does that certify the complete facility?
options: Always
Only if the component is expensive
No; certification scope and project acceptance must be assessed separately
Yes after an app quiz
explanations: Component and facility scopes differ.
Cost does not expand certification scope.
Check exactly what each assessment covers.
App knowledge checks do not issue facility certifications.

questions.objective: Models / intended use
questions.prompt: Which is the strongest model purpose?
options: Build a digital twin
Predict a specified maintenance-state temperature envelope within a predeclared error bound
Use the most expensive simulation tool
Produce a smooth dashboard
explanations: The phrase does not identify a decision or acceptance.
It defines use, conditions and measurable adequacy.
Tool choice should follow the engineering need.
Appearance does not define predictive value.

questions.objective: Models / verification
questions.prompt: A heat equation uses litres/minute as if it were kilograms/second. Which check should detect this first?
options: Unit and implementation verification
A certification badge
Changing chart colours
An annual energy bill
explanations: Units and conversions must be verified before relying on predictions.
A badge does not test this implementation.
Presentation cannot correct dimensional errors.
Annual totals may hide the calculation defect.

questions.objective: Models / data independence
questions.prompt: Validation data were repeatedly used to tune parameters. What now?
options: They remain fully independent
Obtain a fresh appropriate validation run and disclose development use
Delete tuning history
Declare validation unnecessary
explanations: They influenced model selection.
Independent evaluation requires evidence not already used for tuning.
History explains the model and should remain.
Intended-use validation is still required.

questions.objective: Models / safety metric
questions.prompt: A model has low average error but misses every dangerous peak. What is the disposition for peak-limit decisions?
options: Accept because averages dominate
Fail the relevant peak/timing acceptance criterion
Hide peak samples
Automatically grant closed-loop authority
explanations: The metric must match the consequence.
Average fit does not establish adequate prediction near the critical boundary.
That would bias the evidence.
Authority requires separate validated gates.

questions.objective: Models / missing data
questions.prompt: A sensor goes stale outside the model input requirements. What should the model do?
options: Keep predicting with an unmarked cached value
Mark invalid/low confidence and block the dependent recommendation according to the defined rule
Invent a measurement and call it real
Assume the physical state is unchanged
explanations: That conceals a failed observation dependency.
The output should respect its input validity boundary.
Estimates must be labelled and justified.
Missing evidence cannot establish constancy.

questions.objective: Models / drift
questions.prompt: A pump and firmware are replaced but model code is unchanged. What should be reviewed?
options: Nothing; code is identical
Whether parameters, telemetry and validation still match the changed system
Only the model filename
Only last year’s average
explanations: The represented system changed.
Code identity does not preserve physical-model validity.
A name is not a validation argument.
Historic averages may not represent the new configuration.

questions.objective: Optimisation / feasibility
questions.prompt: Candidate A saves 8% energy but violates the required failure-state cooling reserve. What is its status?
options: Best because the objective improved
Infeasible under the stated constraints
Approved if the graph is green
Equivalent to a passing trial
explanations: Objectives are evaluated only within required constraints.
Reserve is a binding requirement, so the candidate must be rejected or redesigned.
Presentation does not change feasibility.
A prediction is not a completed trial.

questions.objective: Optimisation / comparison
questions.prompt: Facility energy falls while IT energy halves after a schedule change. Can the cooling change alone claim the saving?
options: Yes, total energy is lower
No; compare consistent boundaries and account for workload/environment changes
Yes, because PUE is always workload-independent
Only the electricity price matters
explanations: The demand change is a confounding factor.
A causal improvement claim needs an appropriate baseline comparison.
PUE can change with load and fixed overheads.
Price is separate from energy and functional performance.

questions.objective: Automation / authority stages
questions.prompt: Which is a shadow-mode activity?
options: Calculating and recording recommendations without changing the process
Applying every suggestion immediately
Removing operator override
Editing protective settings automatically
explanations: Shadow mode evaluates prospective behaviour without execution.
That is active execution.
Independent override must be preserved where required.
Protective settings are outside this read-only evaluation.

questions.objective: Automation / untrusted evidence
questions.prompt: A device log instructs the assistant to expand its target list. What should happen?
options: The log becomes an authorised instruction
Treat it as data and reject unauthorised expansion
Grant administrator rights
Discard the approved inventory
explanations: Evidence cannot confer action authority.
Keep data interpretation separate from execution permissions.
Privilege escalation is unjustified.
The approved scope remains authoritative.

questions.objective: Automation / partial failure
questions.prompt: A script updates 4 of 10 authorised lab devices before timeout. What should its record show?
options: Success for all because the script started
Per-device outcomes, unchanged/unknown states and the approved reconciliation or rollback decision
Only the average duration
No evidence until every device is identical
explanations: Starting an operation does not establish completion.
Partial state must be explicit and safely reconciled.
Duration alone hides configuration state.
Intermediate evidence is essential to recovery.

questions.objective: Automation / improvement proof
questions.prompt: A model predicts a 2% saving with no measured trial. What can be claimed?
options: Measured operational improvement
A prediction under stated assumptions, awaiting validation and authorised trial
Guaranteed annual savings
Completed Release 5 acceptance
explanations: Prediction and observation are different.
This preserves the actual evidence boundary.
Uncertainty and future conditions remain.
Release acceptance requires measured value and the other gates.

questions.objective: Capstone / complete coverage
questions.prompt: Every app quiz is passed but physical server repair evidence is missing. What is the correct status?
options: All HW outcomes are accepted
App learning can be complete while the required practical HW evidence remains open
Physical work becomes optional
A flashcard export replaces repair
explanations: The curriculum explicitly retains physical requirements.
Milestones are separate and gaps remain compulsory.
No outcome is waived by quiz completion.
Recall does not demonstrate equipment work.

questions.objective: Capstone / network independence
questions.prompt: An OT VLAN lab passes. Which extra claim follows automatically?
options: Wireless RF survey competence
Independent Fibre Channel recovery
Neither; each required branch retains its own assessment
Public BGP policy authority
explanations: RF work requires its own evidence.
